The optional customer_id query param is the only remaining filter, allowing the attacker to enumerate locations for any customer_id across any region. location_out() returns customer_id, name, address, city, state, and postal_code of all locations.

extra.message: CSV import accepts application/octet-stream with no content verification

metadata.citation:
if file.content_type not in {"text/csv", "application/vnd.ms-excel", "application/octet-stream"}:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail="Upload a CSV file")
metadata.proof: POST /api/imports/{kind} accepts content type application/octet-stream which is attacker-controlled. read_csv_upload decodes the raw bytes as UTF-8-SIG and passes to csv.DictReader. An attacker can upload crafted payloads containing formula injection or excessively large datasets for DoS.

extra.message: Export routes loads unbounded rows into memory with no query limit

metadata.proof: GET /api/exports/routes.csv uses .all() with no LIMIT clause. The entire result set is materialized into a Python list then serialized to CSV via StringIO. With thousands of routes each having multiple jobs, this can exhaust server memory. Identical pattern in export_completions (.all() at line ~1452) and export_incidents (.all() at line ~1482).

extra.message: Proof upload validated only by client-supplied Content-Type — no magic-byte verification

metadata.citation:
if file.content_type not in ALLOWED_UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=415, detail="Unsupported proof content type")
metadata.proof: UploadFile.content_type is attacker-controlled via the multipart request header. It is checked against ALLOWED_UPLOAD_CONTENT_TYPES at line 973 which includes application/octet-stream as a catch-all. No magic-byte or MIME-detection is performed. The spoofed content_type is stored verbatim in ProofUpload.content_type (line 990) and served back via FileResponse(media_type=proof.content_type) in download_proof (line 1023). An attacker can upload arbitrary malicious files (executables, HTML, SVG with scripts) by setting Content-Type to an allowed value.

extra.message: Account enumeration via registration — distinct 409 response reveals registered emails

metadata.citation:
if existing:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="An account with this email already exists")
metadata.proof: POST /api/auth/register queries the user by email. If a record exists, it returns HTTP 409 with a distinct message, versus HTTP 200 on success. Unlike login (line 422) and password-reset (line 511) which return uniform messages, this allows attackers to enumerate registered emails by observing the status code.

extra.message: GET /api/admin/users returns all user records without pagination or row limit

metadata.proof: Authenticated admin request to GET /api/admin/users uses query.all() with no LIMIT, OFFSET, cursor, or streaming. Every row from the users table is loaded into a Python list and serialized into a JSON array, causing unbounded memory allocation with many users.

metadata.proof: Authenticated admin/dispatcher request to GET /api/customers uses query.all() with no LIMIT. Contrast with /api/reference which applies .limit(200) on the same pattern (line 616). With many customers this causes unbounded memory consumption.

extra.message: Cross-tenant job mutation via regionless API key

metadata.citation: if api_key.region_id is not None and job.location.region_id != api_key.region_id:
metadata.proof: SOURCE: attacker-supplied x_api_key header and reference in the integration payload. SINK: The region check at line 1678 is skipped entirely when api_key.region_id is NULL, so a regionless API key can update the status of any job by reference across all customers/tenants. Unlike dispatchers (where regionless is an intentional design choice per authz.py), API keys for external integrations have no such design rationale — the regionless bypass is unprotected.

extra.message: Uploaded proof documents stored unencrypted on disk

metadata.proof: SOURCE: file bytes uploaded via POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/proofs (line 968). SINK: target.write_bytes(contents) at line 984 writes the raw bytes directly to UPLOAD_DIR (uploads/proofs) with no encryption at rest. Proof categories include signatures, photos, forms, and completion documents that may contain PII/PHI; anyone with filesystem access can read them.

extra.message: Session bearer tokens stored in plaintext in the database

metadata.proof: SOURCE: token_urlsafe(48) generated during login/register (main.py line 74) and used as the fd_session cookie value. SINK: The UserSession primary key 'id' at models.py line 341 stores the full bearer token verbatim. Unlike API keys, which are hashed with hash_secret() (main.py line 1642), session tokens are not hashed before storage. A database compromise allows an attacker to hijack active sessions by replaying the stored id as the fd_session cookie.
